description:
Mega Man X5 is the fifth entry in Capcom's Mega Man X series, released for the
PlayStation in 2000. Play as X or Zero, defeat eight Mavericks in any order,
and stop the colony drop before Sigma's plan comes to fruition.

mmx5-v0.1.0.description:
> [!WARNING]
> **This build is broken — use [v0.1.2](https://github.com/Shinnuu/Archipelago/releases/tag/mmx5-v0.1.2) instead.** It declares an Archipelago version that was never released, so it will not load at all.

Archipelago support for **Mega Man X5** (PS1, NTSC-U, SLUS-01334). Feature-complete and open for testing while the [upstream PR](https://github.com/ArchipelagoMW/Archipelago/pull/6369) is in review.

Download `mmx5.apworld` below.

## Requirements

- Archipelago **0.6.8+**
- BizHawk **2.7 or newer** (tested on 2.10)
- Your own NTSC-U dump (SLUS-01334) — raw 2352-byte/sector `.bin`, single data track
  - Redump: `98c0d278dc4a795a0a7562d950d37cc9`
  - Same disc with one extra trailing zero sector: `09e670f6e666211b7fcdbb7d48b716e1`
- A PS1 BIOS configured in BizHawk

## Install

1. Drop `mmx5.apworld` into your Archipelago install's `custom_worlds/` folder and restart the Launcher.
2. Generate with a Mega Man X5 YAML (Launcher → Generate Template Options).
3. Open the resulting `.apmmx5` (Launcher → Open Patch). Archipelago asks for your disc image once, then writes a patched `.bin` + `.cue`.
4. Load the **`.cue`** in BizHawk, run `data/lua/connector_bizhawk_generic.lua` in the Lua Console, and connect the BizHawk Client.

The full setup guide ships inside the apworld (`docs/setup_en.md`).

## What's randomized

**45 locations** — the intro clear, and per Maverick stage: the boss, its Heart Tank, its armor capsule, its DNA reward and DNA part, plus the four tank pickups.

**36 items** — 8 special weapons, 8 Heart Tanks, 2 Sub-Tanks, the W-Tank and EX-Tank, all 8 armor parts (Falcon and Gaea), and 4 Enigma + 4 Shuttle launcher parts.

**Goals:** `sigma` (defeat Sigma) or `launch` (collect all 8 launcher parts — a launch only succeeds with the full set).

**Options:** `boss_difficulty` (relaxed / standard / intense) sets the Boss Level base. The collision countdown is frozen, so all 8 stages stay open and backtracking is free.

## Testing status

Verified live: full check-and-item loop on a clean save, Sigma goal completion, weapon/tank/armor/Heart Tank grants, capsule checks with vanilla grants suppressed, and generation including multiworld seeds. The patch pipeline reproduces byte-identical output from either accepted dump.

Not yet exercised: nobody has played the **launch goal** through a complete seed (the mechanism is verified live — a partless launch fails, a full set succeeds — but not a full run), and only single-slot play has happened; multiworld is generation-tested only.

## Notes

- **Everyone in a multiworld needs the same apworld version.** The game edits live in the apworld rather than the seed, so mismatched versions produce a disc that doesn't match the seed's expectations.
- **Armor capsules play Dr. Light's dialogue but grant nothing.** That's correct — the capsule is the check and the part comes from the multiworld. You must walk fully into the capsule; standing beside it opens it but won't continue the sequence.
- **BizHawk only writes the memory card on a clean close or Flush SaveRAM (`Ctrl+S`)** unless you enable autosave. Savestates also carry the memory card.

Bug reports and feedback: [open an issue](https://github.com/Shinnuu/Archipelago/issues).

mmx5-v0.1.1.description:
> [!NOTE]
> **Superseded by [v0.1.2](https://github.com/Shinnuu/Archipelago/releases/tag/mmx5-v0.1.2).** The phantom Intro Clear fix claimed below did not work; v0.1.2 fixes it properly. Everything else here is still valid.

**Replace v0.1.0 with this.** That build could not be used without hand-editing the apworld — thanks to the testers who found it fast.

Download `mmx5.apworld` below and drop it in your Archipelago `custom_worlds/` folder.

## Fixed

- **The world now actually loads.** v0.1.0 required Archipelago `0.6.8`, which is an *unreleased* development version — so Archipelago rejected the world and it never showed up in the game list at all. It now requires **0.6.7**, the current release, verified by generating on it.
- **Seeds now accept normal clients.** The same wrong version was also set as the minimum client version, which the server enforces — every released client would have been refused. Now 0.6.7.
- **`.apmmx5` is registered with the Launcher.** The extension wasn't listed in Open Patch, and "open with → Archipelago Launcher" couldn't route the file, so you were never prompted for your disc image.
- **No more phantom checks.** Check detection could read the save area before a save was actually loaded, so leftover data from a previous session could complete locations — one tester got a spurious "Intro Stage - Clear", which then swallowed the real one when they beat the intro. It could also have falsely completed boss/Heart Tank locations.
- **Much quieter client log.** Repeated disc-mode, save-gate and grant lines are now debug-level.

## Requirements

- Archipelago **0.6.7+**
- BizHawk **2.7 or newer** (tested on 2.10)
- Your own NTSC-U dump (SLUS-01334), raw 2352-byte/sector `.bin`
  - Redump: `98c0d278dc4a795a0a7562d950d37cc9`
  - Same disc with one extra trailing zero sector: `09e670f6e666211b7fcdbb7d48b716e1`
- A PS1 BIOS configured in BizHawk

## Install

1. Put `mmx5.apworld` in `custom_worlds/` and restart the Launcher.
2. Generate with a Mega Man X5 YAML (Launcher → Generate Template Options).
3. Open the `.apmmx5` (Launcher → **Open Patch**). It asks for your disc image once, then writes a patched `.bin` + `.cue`.
4. Load the **`.cue`** in BizHawk, run `data/lua/connector_bizhawk_generic.lua` in the Lua Console, and connect the BizHawk Client.

## Still worth knowing

- **Received items apply at the next stage load**, not instantly — they're written to your save data and the game builds live weapon/armor state when a stage loads. Nothing is lost.
- **Armor capsules play Dr. Light's dialogue but grant nothing.** That's correct: the capsule is the check, the part comes from the multiworld. Walk fully into it — standing beside it won't trigger the sequence.
- **Everyone in a multiworld needs the same apworld version**; the game edits ship in the apworld, not the seed.
- Beating a Maverick sends **three** checks at once (boss, DNA reward, DNA Part).

## Testing status

Verified: loading and generation on a real 0.6.7 release, the full patch pipeline (byte-identical output from either accepted dump), the complete check-and-item loop on a clean save, Sigma goal completion, and all four fixes above under automated regression tests.

Still not exercised end-to-end: a full **launch goal** playthrough, and live **multiworld** play (generation is tested; receiving an item from another slot in a live session is not). Help there is very welcome.

Bug reports: [open an issue](https://github.com/Shinnuu/Archipelago/issues).

mmx5-v0.1.2.description:
**Training mode no longer sends checks.** v0.1.1 said it had fixed the phantom "Intro Stage - Clear" — it hadn't. This release fixes it for real and corrects that claim.

Download `mmx5.apworld` below and drop it in your Archipelago `custom_worlds/` folder. If you are on v0.1.1 you only need this if you intend to touch Training mode; if you are on v0.1.0, upgrade regardless — that build could not load at all.

## What was actually happening

Selecting Training writes story ACT `0x0A` **and** max HP `0x20` into the ordinary save struct in the same frame. v0.1.1 only required the save to *look* loaded, which Training satisfies outright — so the phantom check still went out. The client now recognises the training pseudo-save and suspends **all** checks, item grants and launch pinning until you leave it.

Measured scope, so you know what a Training visit could and could not have done to a seed: the training boss kill sets no progress bits whatsoever, so only the intro location was ever affected — no boss, DNA or Heart Tank check could fire from it. Everything is torn down when you exit Training, so nothing carries into a real session.

v0.1.1's fix was still correct and is still in place; it addressed a different failure — reading the save area before any save exists, e.g. at boot.

## Requirements

- Archipelago **0.6.7+**
- BizHawk **2.7 or newer** (tested on 2.10)
- Your own NTSC-U dump (SLUS-01334), raw 2352-byte/sector `.bin`
  - Redump: `98c0d278dc4a795a0a7562d950d37cc9`
  - Same disc with one extra trailing zero sector: `09e670f6e666211b7fcdbb7d48b716e1`
- A PS1 BIOS configured in BizHawk

## Install

1. Put `mmx5.apworld` in `custom_worlds/` and restart the Launcher.
2. Generate with a Mega Man X5 YAML (Launcher → Generate Template Options).
3. Open the `.apmmx5` (Launcher → **Open Patch**). It asks for your disc image once, then writes a patched `.bin` + `.cue`.
4. Load the **`.cue`** in BizHawk, run `data/lua/connector_bizhawk_generic.lua` in the Lua Console, and connect the BizHawk Client.

## Worth knowing

- **Received items apply at the next stage load**, not instantly. Nothing is lost.
- **Armor capsules play Dr. Light's dialogue but grant nothing** — the capsule is the check, the part comes from the multiworld. Walk fully into it; standing beside it won't trigger the sequence.
- **Everyone in a multiworld needs the same apworld version.**
- Beating a Maverick sends **three** checks at once (boss, DNA reward, DNA Part).

## Testing status

Verified: loading and generation on a real 0.6.7 release, the full patch pipeline, the complete check-and-item loop on a clean save, Sigma goal completion, and every fix in 0.1.1 and 0.1.2 under automated regression tests that are checked to fail against the release they fix.

Still not exercised end-to-end: a full **launch goal** playthrough, and live **multiworld** play. Help there is very welcome.

Bug reports: [open an issue](https://github.com/Shinnuu/Archipelago/issues). The last two releases both came from tester reports — they work.
mmx5-v0.1.2.title: Mega Man X5 apworld v0.1.2 (superseded by v0.1.3)

mmx5-v0.1.3.description:
**Two of these bugs could leave a seed unwinnable. Re-patch your disc with this version.**

Download `mmx5.apworld` below, drop it in `custom_worlds/`, and re-patch — the disc changes in this release (revision 12).

## Fixed

**Tank locations could become permanently uncollectable.** Mega Man X5 deletes any pickup you already own, one frame after it spawns. The client grants tanks by setting exactly those ownership bits — that's what puts a tank in the pause menu — so a Sub-Tank, W-Tank or EX-Tank arriving from the multiworld destroyed the vanilla pickup that *is* that location's check. With progression able to land there, a seed could be stranded. The disc now makes tank pickups ignore ownership; if you're on an older disc, the client works around it until you re-patch. Heart Tanks were never affected.

**Squid Adler's armor capsule could become uncollectable.** Its capsule is opened by collecting the energy balls in the jet-bike section, and owning the part it grants — Falcon Head — makes those balls stop appearing, leaving the capsule sitting there unopenable. The client now holds that one part back while you're in that stage with the capsule uncollected. **This costs you nothing:** the game decides which armor to equip when the stage loads, so armor you have equipped keeps working normally.

**The launch goal could complete without the parts.** Vanilla launches the shuttle by itself once all eight Mavericks are down, and the goal fired on that alone — one tester finished holding 3 of 8 parts. It now requires a successful launch *and* the full set, and tells you your real count in the log if the story's launch goes off early.

## Also

- **`boss_difficulty` is now properly documented** — what relaxed, standard and intense actually do, and why fewer countdown hours means *harder* bosses.
- The Enigma/Shuttle parts screen showing more parts than you received is documented as the cosmetic quirk it is. Only parts you actually received count toward the launch goal.
- Much quieter client log.

## Requirements

- Archipelago **0.6.7+**
- BizHawk **2.7 or newer** (tested on 2.10)
- Your own NTSC-U dump (SLUS-01334), raw 2352-byte/sector `.bin`
  - Redump: `98c0d278dc4a795a0a7562d950d37cc9`
  - Same disc with one extra trailing zero sector: `09e670f6e666211b7fcdbb7d48b716e1`
- A PS1 BIOS configured in BizHawk

## Install

1. Put `mmx5.apworld` in `custom_worlds/` and restart the Launcher.
2. Generate with a Mega Man X5 YAML (Launcher → Generate Template Options).
3. Open the `.apmmx5` (Launcher → **Open Patch**) and point it at your disc image.
4. Load the **`.cue`** in BizHawk, run `data/lua/connector_bizhawk_generic.lua` in the Lua Console, and connect the BizHawk Client.

## Worth knowing

- **A tank or armor part may briefly vanish from your menu.** That's deliberate — the game hides a pickup, or the route to it, once you own what it gives, so the client holds that item back while you're in the stage holding its check. You get it back on collecting the check or leaving.
- **Received items apply at the next stage load**, not instantly.
- **Armor capsules play Dr. Light's dialogue but grant nothing** — the capsule is the check. Walk fully into it.
- **Everyone in a multiworld needs the same apworld version.**
- Beating a Maverick sends **three** checks at once.

## Testing status

Every fix in this release carries an automated regression test that was checked to fail against the release it fixes. Still not exercised end to end: a full **launch goal** playthrough and live **multiworld** play.

Thanks to the testers who found all three of these — every one came from someone playing and reporting. [Issues here](https://github.com/Shinnuu/Archipelago/issues).

mmx5-v0.2.0.description:
First feature release. Three new options, a new default goal, and no known bugs outstanding.

**If you use `text_skip` or `launch_odds`, re-patch your disc.** The new goal does not need one — it is enforced entirely by the client and works on the disc you already have.

## Goal: `all_mavericks` — and it is the new default

Defeat all 8 Mavericks, then Sigma.

Mega Man X5 does not normally require the full set. It opens the endgame as soon as the Eurasia colony situation resolves, and that can happen well before the eighth Maverick — so a run could reach Sigma early, and since Sigma does not respawn, that would end it with the goal unmet. Under this goal the endgame stays shut until all eight are down, and opens on the eighth kill.

`sigma` is unchanged and still available if you prefer the original timing, and `launch` is untouched.

**Seeds generated without an explicit `goal:` line will behave differently to 0.1.3.** Set `goal: sigma` if you want the old default.

## `text_skip` — for when the game yaps

X5 types dialogue one character every 5 frames and then waits for a button on every box. A single line can run past 200 characters — roughly **20 seconds** of typing before you can even press advance.

Turn this on and boxes appear instantly and advance themselves. Cutscenes and Alia's in-stage calls play through with no input at all.

**Choices are not skipped.** Alia's Life Up / Energy Up prompt still stops and waits for you to pick, and the Enigma / Shuttle launch decision is a stage-select menu this never touches. Nothing that affects your run gets answered for you.

Off by default — at this speed the story is unreadable, so leave it off for a first playthrough.

## `launch_odds` — put the gamble back

By default a launch succeeds exactly when you hold all 8 Enigma and Shuttle Parts, and fails otherwise. Set this to `vanilla` and the original game's dice come back:

| | no parts | 1–2 | 3–4 |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Enigma** | 6.25% | 12.5% | 12.5% |
| **Shuttle** | 12.5% | 37.5% | 75% |

(Extra Enigma parts do nothing in the original game either.)

**Under the `launch` goal this can make a seed unwinnable, on purpose.** That goal needs a *successful* launch, you only get two attempts, and even a full set of parts tops out at 75%. Fail both and the colony falls with no third chance. Generation warns you loudly if you pick that combination — it is a gamble with the whole run, not a difficulty slider.

Under `all_mavericks`, no launch can succeed before all 8 Mavericks are down whatever this is set to, since an early success would open the endgame ahead of the goal.

## Requirements

- Archipelago **0.6.7+**
- BizHawk **2.7 or newer** (tested on 2.10)
- Your own NTSC-U dump (SLUS-01334), raw 2352-byte/sector `.bin`
  - Redump: `98c0d278dc4a795a0a7562d950d37cc9`
  - Same disc with one extra trailing zero sector: `09e670f6e666211b7fcdbb7d48b716e1`
- A PS1 BIOS configured in BizHawk

## Install

1. Put `mmx5.apworld` in `custom_worlds/` and restart the Launcher.
2. Generate with a Mega Man X5 YAML (Launcher → Generate Template Options).
3. Open the `.apmmx5` (Launcher → **Open Patch**) and point it at your disc image.
4. Load the **`.cue`** in BizHawk, run `data/lua/connector_bizhawk_generic.lua` in the Lua Console, and connect the BizHawk Client.

## Worth knowing

- **A tank or armor part may briefly vanish from your menu.** Deliberate — the game hides a pickup, or the route to it, once you own what it gives, so the client holds that item back while you are in the stage holding its check. You get it back on collecting the check or leaving.
- **Received items apply at the next stage load**, not instantly.
- **Armor capsules play Dr. Light's dialogue but grant nothing** — the capsule is the check. Walk fully into it.
- **Everyone in a multiworld needs the same apworld version.**
- Beating a Maverick sends **three** checks at once.

## Testing status

Everything here carries automated tests, and the text system and the endgame behaviour were both verified live in an emulator against the real game code.

Not yet exercised end to end: a **full playthrough on any of the new options**, a complete **launch goal** run, and live **multiworld** play. If you hit something odd, please say so — every bug in 0.1.x came from a tester reporting exactly that.
mmx5-v0.2.0.title: Mega Man X5 apworld v0.2.0 (superseded by v0.3.0)

mmx5-v0.3.0.description:
Seven new options. Every one of them has been played in a real game, not just unit-tested.

**Requires Archipelago 0.6.7+.** Drop `mmx5.apworld` in your `custom_worlds/` folder.

## Re-patch your disc? Only if you use pickupsanity

`pickupsanity` changes the disc. Everything else new here is client-side and works on a disc you already patched for 0.2.0.

## One default changed

**`endgame_checks` is ON.** A seed generated without touching it now has **48 locations instead of 45** — clearing Zero Space 1, Zero Space 2 and the X vs Zero fight each send a check. Before this the entire endgame contained nothing to find, so the last stretch of every run was pure travel.

## New options

**`stage_unlocks`** — the eight Maverick stages become progression. One is open at the start, the other seven each need their own "<Boss> Access Codes" item. A locked stage still appears on the stage select and the cursor still moves onto it; pressing confirm just does nothing until its codes arrive.

**`dna_parts_in_pool`** — the equippable DNA Parts become multiworld items. X5 has 16 Parts but a playthrough only ever yields 8, because Alia's Life+ / Energy+ prompt makes you give up one of each Maverick's pair forever. The seed picks one from each pair and shuffles those 8, so which Part you get no longer depends on which prompt you answered.

**`pickupsanity`** — the 32 freestanding Life Energy, Weapon Energy and 1-UP capsules become checks, including the ones in Zero Space and Sigma's stage. Enemy drops are untouched. On these seeds a capsule no longer restores anything when you touch it; the energy it held is in the pool as filler. **Changes the disc.**

**`boss_hp_randomization`** — `weak` 40-80%, `regular` 70-130%, `strong` 120-200%, `chaotic` 25-250%. The roll scales what the game would normally give, so `boss_difficulty` still matters. Rolls are fixed per seed and situation, so dying and retrying gives you the identical fight.

**`secret_armors_in_pool`** — Ultimate Armor and Black Zero shuffled into the pool instead of sitting behind one hidden capsule at the very end. Each only works for its own character, so neither is ever required for anything.

**`randomize_options`** — let the seed pick your gameplay settings. Two results are corrected rather than left to chance: the `launch` goal never comes out paired with vanilla odds (that combination can be unwinnable), and if the roll wants more items than there are locations, `pickupsanity` is switched on to make room.

**`endgame_checks`** — see above.

## Also fixed

- **Generation now refuses option sets that don't fit.** Every item needs a location, and the world wasn't checking. Some combinations produced more items than locations, generated without complaint, and silently dropped items. If a combination is too big you now get a clear error naming the fix instead of a quietly incomplete seed.
- **Received "Small Energy" filler now heals 4 HP** instead of doing nothing.
- **Ultimate Armor is no longer re-asserted after you receive it.** The game writes that byte itself, and the old check would have rewritten it on every later item — which could have reset your armor choice.

## Known

A received armor applies at your **next** stage entry, not the stage you're standing in — the game picks which armor X wears as the stage loads. Black Zero is the exception and applies immediately.

Full detail, including the RAM addresses behind each feature, is in `worlds/mmx5/CHANGELOG.md`.
mmx5-v0.3.0.title: Mega Man X5 apworld v0.3.0 (superseded by v0.3.1)

mmx5-v0.3.1.description:
**Update before you play, and check your disc is actually patched.** This fixes a bug that could corrupt a multiworld for everyone in it.

## What was broken

**If you played on a disc you never patched, the client marked every boss defeated as soon as the weapons arrived.**

It wrote the weapons you received into the same byte the game uses to record boss kills — which is also the byte the client reads to decide what you've beaten. So each weapon sent to you completed that boss's three checks (Boss Defeated, DNA Reward, DNA Part) without you fighting anything. Eight weapons meant **24 false checks**, and in a multiworld those checks released items to everybody else.

Found while investigating a tester report of exactly this symptom. **Whether it caused that particular incident is not settled** — they believe their disc was patched, and the same symptom is reachable another way. This bug is real and reproducible on its own terms, so it is fixed regardless.

## Still open

The only test for "is a save actually loaded" is that max HP reads in a plausible range. RAM left over from a previous game passes that, and RAM survives a soft reset — so stale progress can still be read as real. **If you see phantom checks on a patched disc, please post your client log from `Archipelago/logs/`.** That is what will identify it.

## What changed

**An unpatched disc now holds all checks and items and tells you why**, instead of playing on and quietly breaking things. If you see that message: open your `.apmmx5` with the Archipelago Launcher and load the `.cue` it produces.

This also covers a save already spoiled by an earlier session. The old bug leaves those bits in your save file, and they would otherwise fire again the next time you connected.

**Nothing changes for a correctly patched disc.** Real boss kills still send their checks exactly as before.

## Why it lasted this long

The "unpatched disc" mode predates the disc patch entirely, and the code called it interim. Nothing removed it once patching became the only supported route — and no test could reach it, because the test harness always pretended the disc was patched. Both are fixed.

---

Everything in v0.3.0 is unchanged; see its notes for the seven new options. Requires Archipelago **0.6.7+**.
mmx5-v0.3.1.title: Mega Man X5 apworld v0.3.1 (superseded by v0.3.2)

mmx5-v0.3.2.description:
**Update over v0.3.1.** Second and larger pass at the "checks fire for things you never did" problem.

v0.3.1 closed one route to it. Reviewing that fix turned up two more — and a hole in the fix itself.

## A save carrying progress this seed has never seen is now held

This is the one most likely to have caused the original report, and it defeats both earlier fixes because the save is **genuinely loaded** — nothing about "is this real data" catches it.

A memory card copied from another playthrough, hitting Continue on the wrong slot, or a savestate made before you first connected all look exactly like your own progress, and everything in them would be reported to the multiworld.

If you see **"this save has progress but has never been used with this seed"**, that's this. Start a new game on a fresh slot — or, if you really do mean to bring that save in, the message gives you the exact one-line command to adopt it.

A brand new save is adopted silently the first time it's seen, so a normal run never notices. Clearing the intro doesn't count as progress, so starting the game before you open the client is still fine.

## The "is a save actually loaded" test is much stricter

It now needs the game to be in gameplay, the *previous* poll to have been gameplay too, the relevant bytes identical across both, and a results screen is only believed after real gameplay has been seen.

v0.3.1 required only the first of those, which was weaker than it looked: leftover RAM never changes, so a single poll landing in the right mode was enough to be believed.

## An unpatched disc now really does hold everything

In v0.3.1 the refusal sat *after* the code that grants DNA Parts, locks stages and rerolls boss HP — so an unpatched disc was still being written to. It now happens before anything touches the game, and an unpatched disc can no longer complete the goal either, since finishing releases every remaining location.

## Nothing here costs a correctly patched disc anything

Real progress reports exactly as before.

## Honest limitation

The original report was never traced — the client log that would have named the mechanism wasn't collected. These are three closed routes to one symptom, not a confirmed diagnosis. **If phantom checks ever happen to you, grab the log from `Archipelago/logs/` before anything else.** That's what identifies it.

---

Requires Archipelago **0.6.7+**. Everything from v0.3.0's seven new options is unchanged.
mmx5-v0.3.2.title: Mega Man X5 apworld v0.3.2 (superseded by v0.3.3)

mmx5-v0.3.3.description:
**If you have an unfinished seed using `stage_unlocks`, regenerate it.** A client update cannot rescue an affected seed — the item placement itself is wrong.

## What was broken

A tester's seed put **Dark Dizzy's and Axle the Red's Access Codes inside Sigma's stage.**

To kill those two Mavericks you need their codes. To reach Sigma's stage you need every Maverick dead. There is no way out of that, and generation did not notice — the spoiler's own playthrough "completed" the seed after entering four stages.

## Why

Reaching the endgame required the 8 weapon items. That rule was written when every boss could be reached with no items at all, so weapons were a fine stand-in for progress. Locking the stages broke that assumption, and the rule was never revisited when `stage_unlocks` shipped.

The `all_mavericks` goal is about **kills**; the rule was about **weapons**. Those are only interchangeable while every boss is reachable.

## The fix

The endgame now also requires every Access Codes item, for every goal. Being stricter than the game only limits where items can go; being looser stranded a seed.

Verified on the reporting tester's exact option set: six seeds, no stranded codes, all beatable. Three regression tests, including one that fails if 8 weapons alone ever open the endgame again.

## Checking a seed you already have

Open its spoiler log and look at what sits on the `Sigma - ...` and `Zero Space ... - ...` locations. **If any of them holds an Access Codes item, that seed cannot be finished.** Seeds without `stage_unlocks` were never at risk.

---

Requires Archipelago **0.6.7+**. Everything from v0.3.2 is unchanged.
mmx5-v0.3.3.title: Mega Man X5 apworld v0.3.3 - superseded by v0.3.4

mmx5-v0.3.4.description:
Quality-of-life, all from one tester's completed solo run (`stage_unlocks` + `dna_parts_in_pool` + `pickupsanity`, every check fired correctly).

**Client only — no disc change.** Your existing patched disc and your save carry straight over. Just replace the apworld.

### Weapons now work the moment they arrive

Previously a weapon received mid-stage did nothing until you left and re-entered, which reads exactly like a lost item. Grants are written to your save data, and that is what the game reads when a stage *loads* — the pause menu and the fire button consult a separate live copy that nothing was updating. The client now mirrors granted weapons into it during play.

Armor is still the exception, and that one is the game's design rather than a delay in delivery: X5 decides which armor X wears while the stage is loading, so armor parts and the secret armors take effect at your **next stage entry**.

**Ultimate Armor in particular needs one armorless stage entry to appear** — jumping into an already-cleared stage and leaving again is enough. That has caught several people out, and it is now in the setup guide rather than only in a YAML tooltip.

### Cleared stages get their capsules back (Pickupsanity)

A randomized capsule sends its check instead of restoring energy, and it used to keep doing that for the rest of the run — so revisiting a stage you had already emptied, **the Boss Rush above all**, meant walking past capsules that did nothing.

Now, once **every** pickup check in a stage has been confirmed, that stage's capsules restore energy normally again on a revisit. A stage with any check still outstanding keeps recording. The first collection still never heals you — that energy is in the item pool as filler, which has not changed.

Stages that hold no pickup locations at all — Squid Adler, and the intro — now behave like vanilla too. Suppressing those was never intended.

### Also

- The pickupsanity presence probe now reads the stub's own bytes rather than the dispatch table, which the client rewrites for the change above. Reading its own override back would have switched pickupsanity check detection off for the rest of the session on the next stage exit.
- Setup guide: the "received items appear at the next stage load" and "Small Energy does nothing" notes were both stale and now describe what the client actually does.

### Not fixed yet

The **sub-tank overcap** with received Life Energy, reported at the same time, is not addressed here — it has not been measured, and the right fix depends on what the measurement shows. It is queued.

---

Tests: 300 pass (was 284), release gate 28/28. Requires Archipelago 0.6.7 or newer.
mmx5-v0.3.4.title: Mega Man X5 apworld v0.3.4 - superseded by v0.4.0

mmx5-v0.4.0.description:
Three new options, all client-side — **no disc change**, your existing patched disc and save carry straight over. All three are off by default; turn on what you want in your YAML.  ## Boss Rush rematch checks (`rematch_checks`)  Defeating a Maverick's rematch in Zero Space sends a check — eight new locations, and the most-requested thing testers have asked for: the rush finally rewards something. Nothing is ever lost there: a cleared teleporter stays closed for that visit, but leaving the stage and re-entering resets all eight, so a missed or lost fight can always be redone.  Detection identifies each fight by a fingerprint of the boss code the portal loads. Three of the eight fingerprints are verified in live play (including one full kill → check → item round trip); an unrecognized fight deliberately sends nothing rather than guessing, so the worst a surprise can do is delay one check to the next release. Consider that before placing must-have progression on these in a race.  ## Reploid rescue checks (`reploid_checks`)  Rescuing an injured Reploid sends a check — 14 locations: 6 in Squid Adler, 3 in Izzy Glow, 5 in The Skiver. (Izzy Glow has a third Reploid most people never find — the placement data says where, and yes, it's real; we checked.) Reploids respawn on every stage re-entry, so nothing is permanently missable.  One quirk: a rescue while you already have 9 lives cannot be detected — re-enter with an open life slot and rescue again. Izzy Glow's and The Skiver's Reploids are verified on-screen; Squid Adler's six ship from disc data with the same signature. If one of them misbehaves, report it and it will be fixed in a release.  ## All 16 DNA Parts (`dna_parts_in_pool: all`)  The option is now a choice: `vanilla_pairs` keeps the previous behavior (one Part from each boss's Life+/Energy+ pair; `true` in an old YAML still means this), and `all` shuffles every one of the 16 Parts into the pool — both halves of every pair, an economy the base game never allows. `all` adds 16 items, so the seed needs location budget: `rematch_checks`, `reploid_checks` and/or `pickupsanity` make room, and generation refuses loudly if it doesn't fit.  ---  Install: put `mmx5.apworld` in your Archipelago `custom_worlds` folder. Needs Archipelago 0.6.7+. Full details in the changelog and setup guide inside the package.  

---

**Added 2026-08-09: MMX5-Unpatcher.exe** - a standalone tool (no Archipelago needed) that restores any AP-patched X5 disc to a byte-verified clean dump. Drag a patched .bin onto it, or run it for a file picker; the restored copy is written next to the file and your input is never modified. For anyone who lost track of their clean dump.
mmx5-v0.4.0.title: Mega Man X5 apworld v0.4.0 - superseded by v0.4.1

mmx5-v0.4.1.description:
Patching quality-of-life. **No disc change** — discs and saves from 0.3.x/0.4.0 carry straight over. Needs Archipelago 0.6.7+.

## MMX5-Unpatcher (standalone tool)

`MMX5-Unpatcher.exe`, attached below, restores any AP-patched X5 disc to a **byte-verified clean dump** — for anyone who lost track of their original. Drag a patched `.bin` onto it, or double-click for a file picker. Your input file is never modified; the restored copy is written next to it and md5-verified against the known clean dumps before anything is written. Standalone — it does not need Archipelago installed.

(If Windows Defender gives the exe a suspicious look: that's a common false positive for single-file Python executables, not malware.)

## Smarter patching errors

The most common cause of "recent patches don't work" is pointing the patcher at an **already-patched** disc from an earlier seed. The patcher now detects that and tells you exactly what's wrong and how to fix it — point the base-image setting back at your clean dump (or use the unpatcher above) — instead of a cryptic hash-mismatch error. **You never need to delete anything to re-patch.**

## Worth knowing: you usually don't need to re-patch at all

The disc only changes with three options: `pickupsanity`, `text_skip` and `launch_odds`. Two seeds with the same values for those produce **byte-identical discs** — keep one patched disc per option combo and reuse it. Reusing a disc also keeps its memory card, since BizHawk keys saves to the disc filename.

---

Install: put `mmx5.apworld` in your Archipelago `custom_worlds` folder. Full details in the changelog and setup guide inside the package.
mmx5-v0.4.1.title: Mega Man X5 apworld v0.4.1 - superseded by v0.5.0

mmx5-v0.5.0.description:
Four bug fixes from testers' runs on 0.4.1.

## Do I need to re-patch?

**Only if you use `pickupsanity`.** That option's disc edit changed. Every
other seed produces a byte-identical disc to 0.4.1, and your save carries over
either way.

If you do need to re-patch and you no longer have a clean dump, grab
**MMX5-Unpatcher.exe** below and drag your patched .bin onto it.

## Fixes

**Enemy health drops work again under `pickupsanity`.** Health and weapon
energy dropped by enemies did nothing for most of a stage, then mysteriously
started working once you'd collected every pickup in it. The randomizer hooks
item collection by item *type*, and an enemy's drop is the same type as a
placed capsule, so the hook was swallowing both — it only got out of the way
once a stage had no checks left to record. It now tells them apart and hands
anything an enemy dropped straight back to the game. This is why `pickupsanity`
felt harsher than intended: for most of every stage you were playing with enemy
healing switched off.

**Rematch checks no longer credit the wrong boss.** Boss Rush runs handed out
Squid Adler's and The Skiver's checks for fights that never happened, then gave
nothing when those bosses were actually beaten. Fights were identified by a
16-byte fingerprint of the boss's code, and those two values turned out not to
be unique to their bosses at all — The Skiver's is an ordinary function ending
followed by the next function's beginning, which occurs 40 times on the disc.
Fights are now identified by a 256-byte window, checked to occur exactly once
on the entire disc for all eight bosses, and a kill only counts if the client
watched that boss's health bar fill first.

**Boss health bars stop breaking on low rolls.** With `boss_hp_randomization`
on, a boss rolled below 32 HP drew a corrupt bar: the game builds it from
pre-rendered pieces that only reach down to 32. Rolls now stop at 32 — and
never above the HP the boss would have had anyway, so `weak` stays weak.

**Zero Space is no longer touched by boss HP randomization.** The Boss Rush
rematches don't read their HP from the byte that option changes, so randomizing
it never altered those fights — it only made their health bars disagree with
their actual health. Sigma shares that stage and keeps his normal HP too.

## Testing

398 unit tests, release gate 30/30. The enemy-drop fix was confirmed live on a
real patched disc. The rematch-identity and lifebar changes are covered by unit
tests, mutation testing, and a check that re-derives the fingerprint table from
a real disc — but were not replayed live before release. If you hit something
odd in the Boss Rush or on a low-HP boss, please say so.
mmx5-v0.5.0.title: Mega Man X5 apworld v0.5.0 - superseded by v0.5.1

mmx5-v0.5.1.description:
Fixes a crash. **Client only — no disc change, no re-patch, saves carry over.**

## Gaea Armor no longer crashes the game when you switch weapons

Gaea Armor can't use special weapons, and the game enforces that by clearing
your equipped weapon list when a stage loads. Since 0.3.4 the client has been
mirroring your received weapons back into that list, so a weapon that arrives
mid-stage works right away — and it was doing that under Gaea too, putting the
game into a state it's never meant to reach. Pressing L1/R1 from there crashed
it.

The mirror now leaves Gaea Armor alone. Your weapons are untouched and work
normally again the moment you use any other armor.

**This isn't limited to `secret_armors_in_pool`** — any seed where you collect
all four Gaea parts could hit it. Present in 0.3.4 through 0.5.0.

Reported by a tester on 0.4.1. Thanks for chasing it down.
mmx5-v0.5.1.title: Mega Man X5 apworld v0.5.1 - superseded by v0.5.2

mmx5-v0.5.2.description:
**Client only — no re-patch, saves carry over.**

## Reploid rescues no longer vanish near the life cap

A tester found two Reploids in The Skiver's stage that gave no check — and
made no rescue sound when touched. That turned out to be the game itself: the
rescue routine adds a life, and if that would take you past 9 it clamps back
to 9 and skips the sound, while still using the Reploid up for that visit. No
life, no sound, no check — and re-entering the stage does exactly the same
thing, so the check was effectively uncollectable.

The client now keeps just enough room on your life counter as you approach a
Reploid you still need, so the rescue always registers. Where several sit
close together — Squid Adler's cluster of three, The Skiver's two pairs — it
frees enough for all of them, because rescuing two in quick succession would
otherwise put the second one straight back at the cap.

You may see your life counter dip by one or two near a Reploid. That's this
working. Rescuing hands the lives straight back, so unless you walk away
without taking them you end up where you started.

**If you have Reploid checks that never fired on an earlier run, they're
still there** — re-enter the stage and rescue again.
mmx5-v0.5.2.title: Mega Man X5 apworld v0.5.2 - superseded by v0.5.3

mmx5-v0.5.3.description:
**Re-patch required.** Exit Stage Anytime is on by default and changes the
disc, so you need a fresh `.apmmx5` and a re-patch even if you change nothing
else. Your save carries over. Lost your clean dump? **MMX5-Unpatcher.exe**
below restores any patched disc.

## New: Exit Stage Anytime

The pause menu's "Exit Stage" normally only appears once you have already
beaten that stage's boss — which is backwards here. A randomized run is full
of trips into a stage for one check you can now reach, and of entries into a
stage you cannot finish yet, and leaving used to mean dying on purpose or
clearing a stage you did not come for.

The intro stage and Zero Space stay excluded, exactly as in the base game.
On by default.

## New: Water Stage Speed

Duff McWhalen's forced-scrolling chase moves at a fixed pace you cannot
outrun, which is a long wait every time you re-enter that stage for a check.
Set it to 1.25x, 1.5x or about 1.9x. Off by default.

## Fixed: capsules you have already checked now heal you

Previously this could only be decided a whole stage at a time — every energy
capsule in a stage stayed inert until *all* of that stage's checks were done.
That caused two separate complaints:

- a capsule you had already collected stayed dead for the rest of the run,
  which made revisits, and the Boss Rush especially, a slog;
- in a multiworld, when another player finishes, the server marks the
  locations holding *their* items as checked in your world too. Those capsules
  were then eaten with no health and no check, and the client would announce a
  stage was fully collected while you stood next to capsules you had never
  touched.

The disc now decides capsule by capsule: anything already checked — by you or
by someone else's collect — behaves like a normal energy capsule again, while
the ones still worth a check keep being checks.

---

*Exit Stage and the water-stage speed were located with the help of the
Mega Man X5 Improvement Project Addendum's research workbook; the edits
themselves are derived from the vanilla game.*
mmx5-v0.5.3.title: MMX5 apworld v0.5.3 (superseded by v0.5.4)

mmx5-v0.5.4.description:
Two fixes and two new options. **No re-patch needed** unless you turn on one of the new options — both are off by default and the fixes are client-side, so a disc patched for 0.5.3 is still correct.

## Fixed

**Life Energy you receive now actually heals you.** It never did. The client was writing received energy into what it took for the game's refill queue; those bytes are in fact the fill levels of Sub-Tank 1 and Sub-Tank 2. So the energy healed nothing at any HP — it went into a sub-tank instead, the *wrong* one whenever you were playing Zero, and into a tank you might not even own, in which case it went nowhere at all.

Energy now behaves like a capsule off the floor: it heals you, and at full health it tops up a sub-tank you own. Tanks that the old bug overfilled past the game's own maximum are repaired on sight — that was the sub-tank overcap reported back on 0.5.0.

**A Boss Rush rematch could be credited without fighting it.** A player game-overed out of the Duff McWhalen rematch, came back to the Sigma stage, picked up an item, and was handed the McWhalen rematch check. The address watched for boss HP is not boss-only — it belongs to the game's first object slot, which holds the boss during a rematch and ordinary objects the rest of the time. An object appearing there and going away looks exactly like a boss filling its health bar and dying. The client now checks that the thing in that slot is actually the boss whose code is loaded.

On a multiworld this was worse than a free check, since it releases someone else's item — worth a look at your seed if you saw a rematch complete on its own.

## New options

**Weapon Damage** — randomizes how hard *your* weapons hit. `weak` 50–90% of normal, `regular` 80–130%, `strong` 120–200%, `chaotic` 25–250%. Each weapon rolls once and keeps its shape: a charged shot scales with its uncharged shot, so it can never come out weaker than the plain one.

**Boss Damage** — the mirror, for the eight Mavericks' attacks. Each boss rolls once, so its light pokes stay light next to its big attack and the whole fight gets more or less dangerous together. Attacks shared with ordinary enemies are untouched, and so are instant kills.

Both change the disc, so re-patch if you turn one on. They stack with Boss HP Randomization — `weak` weapons against `strong` bosses is a long afternoon.

## Also

The setup guide was wrong about armor parts: they do nothing individually, and once you hold all four X5 grants the armor on a **results screen** — so the fourth part needs a stage cleared before the armor is selectable.

---

`mmx5.apworld` goes in your Archipelago install's `custom_worlds/` folder. `MMX5-Unpatcher.exe` restores an AP-patched disc to a clean dump if you have lost your original — drag a `.bin` onto it.

Requires Archipelago 0.6.7 or newer. 521 tests, release gate 31/31.
mmx5-v0.5.4.title: MMX5 apworld v0.5.4 (superseded by v0.6.0)

mmx5-v0.6.0.description:
One new feature, and an unpatcher you should update. **No re-patch needed** unless you set a colour — leave them alone and the disc is byte-identical to what 0.5.4 produced, so an existing patched disc and an in-flight seed both stay valid.

## New: player colours

X, Zero, Falcon Armor, Gaea Armor and Ultimate Armor can each be recoloured independently, from 18 presets or `random`. Purely cosmetic — no logic, items or locations are touched, and two players in the same multiworld can pick different colours.

> crimson · scarlet · amber · gold · olive · forest · emerald · teal · cyan · azure · blue · indigo · violet · magenta · rose · silver · black · white

**This is the only setting that is not in your YAML.** Colours live in Archipelago's own `host.yaml` under `mmx5_options`, and are applied while the patch is being opened:

```yaml
mmx5_options:
  rom_file: "Megaman X5.bin"
  x_palette: gold
  zero_palette: violet
  falcon_palette: vanilla
  gaea_palette: vanilla
  ultimate_palette: vanilla
```

That means changing your mind never costs a new seed — but it is not a live toggle either. Set them **before** you open the patch. To change them afterwards, edit `host.yaml`, **delete the `.bin` and `.cue` you made last time**, and open the same `.apmmx5` again. If you skip the delete, the patcher sees a disc of that name already sitting there, does nothing, and does not warn you.

Deleting the old disc and re-patching to the same filename is deliberate: BizHawk keys memory cards and savestates to the disc's filename, so keeping the name keeps your saves.

Presets keep each colour's original brightness and change only hue and saturation, so shading and outlines survive rather than going flat. Faces and skin are never repainted, and Zero keeps his blond hair and his helmet crystal.

**Fourth Armor has no setting of its own** — it is different artwork drawn from X's palette, so `x_palette` recolours it too. Confirmed in game rather than assumed.

## Update your unpatcher

**`MMX5-Unpatcher.exe` is v1.1 and you want it if you use colours.** It now restores the palette records as well, so a recoloured disc still unpatches back to a byte-verified clean dump. The v1.0 build cannot: it would fail its md5 check and refuse to write, leaving you unable to recover your dump from a recoloured disc. If you never touch the colour settings, v1.0 remains correct.

## Also

The setup guide has a new section covering the colour options, how to change them afterwards, and why that step differs from every other setting. It ships as `MMX5-Setup-Guide.pdf` here, so you can read it before installing anything.

---

`mmx5.apworld` goes in your Archipelago install's `custom_worlds/` folder. `MMX5-Unpatcher.exe` restores an AP-patched disc to a clean dump if you have lost your original — drag a `.bin` onto it.

Requires Archipelago 0.6.7 or newer. 540 tests, release gate 37/37.
mmx5-v0.6.0.title: MMX5 apworld v0.6.0 (superseded by v0.6.1)

mmx5-v0.6.1.description:
**Player colours move into your YAML.**

0.6.0 put them in `host.yaml`, and the feedback was consistent: people did not
want to edit a file they had never opened, and several never found out the
feature existed at all — `host.yaml` settings do not appear on the website
generator.

So the five colours (X, Zero, Falcon, Gaea and Ultimate) are ordinary options
now. They show up on the generator with everything else, a typo is refused when
the seed is generated instead of quietly falling back to vanilla, and your
colour is recorded in the spoiler.

## Nothing breaks, and nothing needs regenerating

- **A colour already set in `host.yaml` keeps working exactly as before.** It
  is an override now, and it still wins.
- **YAMLs written for 0.6.0 still generate.** The new options default to
  vanilla.
- You only need a new seed if you want your colour to come from the YAML.
  Anyone mid-seed can keep changing colours by re-patching, as now.

## Two details worth knowing

`random` is rolled when the seed is generated now, rather than from your player
name. Your colour is fixed and appears in the spoiler. It picks from the whole
list, so it can land on vanilla.

**`vanilla` in `host.yaml` does not override anything.** It means "nothing set
here". Archipelago writes those entries into your `host.yaml` by itself with
`vanilla` already in them, so honouring it as a real choice would have quietly
overridden the YAML of every existing player. To play in vanilla colours, pick
`vanilla` in your YAML.

---

`mmx5.apworld` goes in your Archipelago install's `custom_worlds/` folder.
`MMX5-Unpatcher.exe` restores an AP-patched disc (recoloured or not) to a clean
dump if you have lost your original — drag a `.bin` onto it. It is unchanged
from 0.6.0 and you do not need to replace it.
`MMX5-Setup-Guide.pdf` is the setup guide, readable before anything is
installed.

Requires Archipelago 0.6.7 or newer. 563 tests, release gate 37/37.

All MMX5 releases: https://github.com/Shinnuu/Archipelago/releases?q=mmx5
mmx5-v0.6.1.title: MMX5 apworld v0.6.1

mmx5-v0.6.2.description:
**Exit Stage now works in every stage, and escaping Zero Space is safe.**

Exit Stage was only ever offered in the eight Maverick stages — that is the
range vanilla's own check uses, and the randomizer had only removed vanilla's
*other* condition, the one that made you beat the stage first. A playtester
found the gap the obvious way, in Zero Space 2. It now covers the Enigma and
Shuttle sorties, Sigma's stage and all of Zero Space too.

**The intro stage is still excluded**, deliberately: leaving it early strands
your story progress, and there is no stage select to go back to yet.

## Escaping Zero Space does not skip it

0.6.2 was going to ship with a caution here. The game picks which Zero Space
stage comes next from a counter it advances as you leave one, and vanilla can
never escape those stages, so there was no established behaviour to rely on —
escaping *might* have counted as passing the stage and skipped the check inside
it.

It does not. An escape leaves that counter untouched, and the stage and its
check are still there to come back to. Measured on a real disc, twice in Zero
Space 1 and twice in an uncleared Maverick stage. Escape freely.

## Fixed: with Stage Unlocks on, entering a stage could drop you into a different one

Reported live — pick Squid Adler, back out at the character select, then enter
Mattrex, and the game loaded Squid Adler.

The stage select writes your destination into memory the moment you confirm,
and the game does not read it back until the loading screen. In between sit the
zoom, the character select and the back-out, and the randomizer was writing
into that byte during all of it. It had one legitimate reason to: confirming a
locked stage leaves a value there the game never writes itself, and the
randomizer puts a sane one back. But it was putting back *the last stage it had
seen you choose* rather than the hub, and deciding to do so from a reading
taken a fraction of a second earlier — so a stage you picked before could land
on top of the one you had just picked.

It now writes only while you are actually on the stage-select cursor, only the
hub's own value, and only after checking the byte still needs it. Nothing about
how Stage Unlocks plays has changed; locked stages still do nothing on confirm,
exactly as before.

## What you need to do

**Re-patch.** This changes the disc. Generate a fresh `.apmmx5`, re-patch, and
carry on — your save and any in-flight seed are unaffected.

**Replace `MMX5-Unpatcher.exe` as well.** Unlike 0.6.1, this one is not
optional: 0.6.2 edits a disc location earlier unpatchers do not know about, so
an older one will refuse a 0.6.2 disc rather than restore it. The version here
handles every AP disc revision to date, this one included.

---

`mmx5.apworld` goes in your Archipelago install's `custom_worlds/` folder.
`MMX5-Unpatcher.exe` restores an AP-patched disc (recoloured or not) to a clean
dump if you have lost your original — drag a `.bin` onto it.
`MMX5-Setup-Guide.pdf` is the setup guide, readable before anything is
installed.

Requires Archipelago 0.6.7 or later.
mmx5-v0.6.2.title: MMX5 apworld v0.6.2

mmx5-v0.7.0.description:
**Three new options: stage music, starting life, and what a Heart Tank is worth.**

## `stage_music` — shuffle the music between stages

The thirteen themes the stages already use are dealt back out among them, so
every stage still gets a real stage theme, every theme is still used somewhere,
and no stage keeps the one it started with. Seventeen places, thirteen themes,
so four themes turn up twice.

Places that merely *shared* music in the base game are split: Zero Space 1,
Zero Space 2 and the X-vs-Zero duel each get their own theme, and so do the
Enigma and Shuttle sorties.

**Only stages change.** The hub, the stage select, cutscenes, results and
transition screens, every jingle and the ending keep their vanilla music. That
is structural rather than a curated exclusion list — the game picks stage music
through a cue table indexed by stage id, and only the rows that are stages are
rewritten.

Purely cosmetic: it moves no checks and changes no logic.

## `starting_hp` — how much life X and Zero begin with

Vanilla is 32; anything from 1 to 127 is allowed. 127 is the ceiling because
the game reads the maximum with a *signed* byte load, so 128 would read as
negative.

Applied to a **new save**, once, the first time the client adopts it. Life the
game itself granted you — Alia's Life Up rewards, which are not Archipelago
items — is kept rather than overwritten.

**Above 64 the life bar overflows its own frame.** The frame has seventeen
sizes covering 32 to 64 and stops growing there while the fill keeps going.
That is how the genre draws a bar past its vanilla maximum, the extra life is
real, and it is deliberately left alone.

**Below 32 needed a disc fix.** The frame is a sprite index clamped at the top
and *not* at the bottom, so a maximum under 32 indexed off the front of the
artwork and drew unrelated HUD elements. Both copies of that code now floor the
index at the smallest real bar.

## `heart_tank_value` — what each Heart Tank is worth

Vanilla is 2. 0 makes them worth nothing while the check still sends. The total
now stops at 127 rather than at vanilla's 64, which also fixes a quieter bug:
Heart Tanks received past a maximum of 64 used to be silently worth nothing.

Alia's Life Up rewards are **not** affected — they stay worth 2 each on top of
whatever you set. Client-side, so it works on a disc you have already patched.

## Fixed: a save could stop sending checks without saying so

The client decided whether a save was resident by checking its maximum life
against a fixed 16–64 window. Both new life options can legitimately leave that
window, and a save judged not resident goes quiet. The window is now derived
from the seed.

## What you need to do

**Re-patch only if you turn on `stage_music`, or set `starting_hp` below 32.**
Everything else here is client-side. A seed using neither produces a disc
byte-identical to 0.6.2's, so it needs nothing — carry on with the disc you
have.

**Replace `MMX5-Unpatcher.exe` if you do re-patch.** This release edits disc
locations earlier unpatchers do not know about, so an older one refuses a 0.7.0
disc rather than restoring it. The version here (v1.2) handles every AP disc
revision to date, this one included.

---

`mmx5.apworld` goes in your Archipelago install's `custom_worlds/` folder.
`MMX5-Unpatcher.exe` restores an AP-patched disc (recoloured or not) to a clean
dump if you have lost your original — drag a `.bin` onto it.
`MMX5-Setup-Guide.pdf` is the setup guide, readable before anything is
installed.

Requires Archipelago 0.6.7 or later.
mmx5-v0.7.0.title: MMX5 apworld v0.7.0

mmx5-v0.7.1.description:
**Fixes a freeze: maximum life could overflow, taking the HUD with it.**

Reported from a live seed in Zero Space — frozen at the spawn point, HUD tiles
painted across the screen, weapon menu still working, the other character fine.

**No re-patch.** This is client-side only. Update the apworld and carry on with
the disc you have.

## What was happening

The apworld's own life grants stop at 127, which is the most the game can hold.
The game's *own* grants do not check: Alia's Life Up reward and the vanilla
Heart Tank pickup each add 2 with no ceiling, because vanilla tops out at 64
and never needed one.

Landing on top of a maximum already at 127, they pushed the byte to 129 — and
the life bar reads that byte as **signed**, so 129 read as −127 and the bar's
frame index landed 79 frames off the front of its own artwork, drawing whole
sheets of unrelated tiles over the screen. You could still open the weapon
menu; you could not move.

Those grants raise only the character you are playing, which is why the other
one was untouched and still playable.

## The quieter half

An overflowed maximum also failed the client's "is a save resident" test, so
the client stopped sending checks and said nothing about it — and every path
that could have repaired the save ran behind that same test, which is why it
could not recover on its own.

## What changed

The client corrects the maximum back to 127 as soon as it sees it, ahead of
the residency test, so checks keep flowing through the same poll. It restores
the life you were left with, and **a save that has already broken is repaired
on connect** — an affected run does not need restarting.

`heart_tank_value` totals now stop at 127 *including* Alia's Life Ups, rather
than letting hers push past it.

Only reachable for seeds with a high `starting_hp` or `heart_tank_value`; a
default seed could never get near it.

---

`mmx5.apworld` goes in your Archipelago install's `custom_worlds/` folder.
`MMX5-Unpatcher.exe` is unchanged from 0.7.0 (v1.2) — keep the one you have.
`MMX5-Setup-Guide.pdf` is the setup guide.

Requires Archipelago 0.6.7 or later.

mmx5-v0.7.2.description:
Three fixes from one player report, plus a change that makes the next report easier to read.

**Most of this needs no re-patch** — update the apworld and carry on with the disc you have. The one exception is the launcher-part fix, which is in generation, so it applies to **seeds rolled from 0.7.2 onward**; a seed already in flight keeps the placements it was rolled with.

## Fixed: the life-overflow repair could not fire where the overflow happens

0.7.1 shipped a fix for maximum life overflowing past the value the life bar can read. The same bug was reported three days later: cleared Zero Space 1, loaded into Zero Space 2, frozen at the spawn point with the life bar showing a single point.

The repair only ran while the game was in gameplay or on the results screen — and endgame stages do not use the results screen at all. The client log shows the maximum going to 129 within 0.6 seconds of the Zero Space 1 clear, after which the game walked cutscene → stage select → stage entry → frozen, never once passing through a state the repair was allowed to run in. It had been gated on the one condition the bug prevents.

It now runs wherever the bad byte is found, so it is corrected before the next stage can load and copy it into your live health. **A save that is already broken is fixed the moment you connect**, from the menus, without having to reach a stage first.

The repair also used to give up above 159 — a guess at how much life the game could hand out behind the client's back. Nothing counts those grants or limits them, so all that ceiling guaranteed was that a save which drifted further could never be rescued. Any maximum above 127 is now put back.

## Fixed: Enigma and Shuttle Parts could be placed in the endgame

*(Needs a new seed.)*

The parts decide whether the colony launch succeeds, and the launch resolves **before** Zero Space opens — the game fires the shuttle by itself once all eight Mavericks are down. A part inside Zero Space or Sigma's stage is therefore behind the one event it exists to affect. Reported from a live `sigma`-goal seed whose last Shuttle Part was a Zero Space check: the launch fired on schedule, failed for want of that part, and the part was sitting on the far side of the endgame it had just failed to open.

Under `sigma` and `all_mavericks` nothing objected, because the parts are only *useful* there — the seed was winnable and the player simply lost the successful-launch route with no way to tell why.

Launcher parts are now kept out of every endgame location, under every goal, and out of every **other** Mega Man X5 slot's endgame too — two X5 players both reach Zero Space only after their own launch has already fired.

Measured on six seeds rolled from the reporter's own YAML: 48 part placements, none in an endgame location. Without the fix, on those same six seeds, 16 of the 48 landed there.

## Fixed: a held-back armor part was not given back until your next item

Owning Falcon Head hides the energy balls that open Squid Adler's capsule, so while you are in that stage the client holds that one part back. It stops as soon as the capsule check is collected or you leave — but nothing actually put the part back. It stayed missing until the next item arrived from the multiworld, and saving in that window wrote a memory card without it. It is now restored the moment the hold ends.

Related: the armor-set completion flags were pinned once per client session rather than once per visit, so returning to Squid Adler much later could push those flags back to what they were on your first visit — possibly before you had finished another armor set. They are now re-read each visit.

**If you saw Squid Adler's energy balls missing and had never opened that capsule:** that is expected once the check has already been banked, and Archipelago banks it for you automatically when another player in your multiworld finishes and collects — their auto-collect marks every location holding their items as checked, yours included. The location was complete and nothing was lost; the orbs had nothing left to guard.

## Added: the client log now names the apworld version and your options

Bug reports arrive as client logs, and until now a log said which Archipelago the launcher was but never which version of this world — so answering "which release was this?" meant guessing from behaviour. One line at connect now carries the world version, seed, slot and every option the client acts on.
